practices.practice: For Python apps prefer one process-global AsyncMongoClient (PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient) reused across the app lifecycle rather than creating a new Motor AsyncIOMotorClient per request; initialize once and close on shutdown.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code it; create a single AsyncIOMotorClient per process and reuse it for all Beanie/ODM operations (close it on shutdown).

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string and other secrets from environment variables or a secure secret store (Key Vault) and provide a `.env.example` placeholder for local/dev only; never commit real secrets to source control.
practices.prior_belief: Store secrets (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY) in environment variables or a secrets store; never commit keys to source control and provide a .env.example placeholder file.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS (tls=true) and do not disable certificate verification in production; fix CA bundle/SNI issues rather than allowing invalid certificates.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL on the Mongo client connection (tls=true) and verify server certificates; do not disable certificate verification in production.

practices.practice: Tune Mongo client pool and timeout parameters for the deployment model (serverless: small pools, short maxIdleTimeMS; long-running servers: larger maxPoolSize and longer maxIdleTimeMS) and set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS to reasonable values for your environment.
practices.prior_belief: Tune Mongo client pool and timeouts: set a sensible maxPoolSize for expected concurrency and configure serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS to avoid long blocking calls.

practices.practice: Avoid logging or printing full connection strings and API keys; use Key Vault/managed identities and secret-scanning tools, and keep `.env` out of source control.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid logging or printing the full connection string or API keys; redact sensitive fields if connection strings must be shown in logs.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB connection string environment variable best practices

practices.practice: Use a durable unique key (e.g., review_id or _id) and create a unique index on it so upserts are idempotent.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single durable unique key for each review (review_id or _id) and create a unique index on it to make upserts idempotent (use update_one/replace_one with upsert=True).

practices.practice: Model sentiment as a numeric field (e.g., float) and store tags as a bounded array of strings, and be aware multikey indexes create one index entry per array element so index tags selectively and keep arrays bounded or move to a child collection.
practices.prior_belief: Model sentiment as a numeric field (e.g., sentiment_score float normalized to -1..1 or 0..1) and store tags as a small array of strings (tags: ["feature", "delivery"]). Index sentiment or tags selectively based on query patterns.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB enforces the MongoDB BSON document size limit (16 MB); keep documents well under 16 MB and spill large fields to a side collection or external blob storage.
practices.prior_belief: Keep document sizes small (well below 2 MB); store large assets externally (blob storage) and keep references in the document to reduce RU cost and avoid item-size limits.

practices.practice: Create indexes to support aggregation/reporting: at minimum index product_id and create a compound index on (product_id, sentiment) when grouping by product and sentiment to accelerate aggregation pipelines.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes to support your aggregation/reporting: at minimum index product_id and sentiment (or a compound index on (product_id, sentiment)) to accelerate GROUP BY product+sentiment aggregation pipelines.

practices.practice: Avoid unnecessary indexes: maintain a modest index budget (e.g., 5–15 indexes per collection), review index usage with $indexStats, and prefer partial/sparse indexes to reduce write and storage cost.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid unnecessary indexes (each index increases RU cost and storage); measure index usage and drop unused indexes. Create sparse or partial indexes when appropriate to reduce index size.

practices.practice: When creating a vector index declare the field dimensions and index kind (vector-diskann, vector-hnsw or vector-ivf) and choose the similarity metric (COS/IP/L2); prefer DiskANN for large production workloads.
practices.prior_belief: If using vector search, declare the vector field with its dimensionality and create a vector index specifying algorithm (e.g., hnsw or ivf), metric (cosine/inner_product), and tuning parameters (M, efConstruction, nlist, efSearch) appropriate for recall/latency tradeoffs.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings at ingestion when using cosine similarity and store embedding model name and dimensions with the vector to detect model drift and support re-embedding.

When running vector KNN queries tune query-time parameters (k, lSearch/efSearch), combine vector retrieval with pre-filters, and project only required fields and limit returned neighbors to reduce RU/latency.
practices.prior_belief: When performing vector queries, project only required fields and limit the number of returned neighbors; use efSearch or query-time parameters to balance accuracy and RU/latency.

practices.practice: Implement application retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (network blips, 429 throttling, transient 5xx), and honour Retry-After headers when present.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (network errors, 429 throttling, transient 5xx responses); detect rate-limiting responses and respect Retry-After headers where provided.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB does not support driver-level retryable writes (connection strings often set retryWrites=false); do not rely on automatic retryable-write semantics—implement safe application-level retries instead.
Provision throughput by choosing appropriate compute tier and storage (use autoscale or pick a tier sized for peak ingestion/aggregation); monitor RU consumption and scale or change tier proactively.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput to avoid throttling: use autoscale RU/s or database/container-level provisioned throughput sized for peak ingestion and aggregation workloads; monitor RU consumption and scale proactively.

practices.practice: Write aggregation pipelines to be RU-efficient: $match early, $project early, avoid $lookup where possible, and design $group on indexed fields; test RU cost with explain and adjust.
practices.prior_belief: Design aggregation pipelines to be RU-efficient: project early ($project), filter early ($match), avoid $lookup where possible, and use $group on indexed fields when feasible; test pipeline RU cost with real data.

practices.practice: Use pagination and batching (cursor + limit / batchSize) for reads to avoid scanning large collections in a single request; prefer cursor-based paging for large datasets.
practices.prior_belief: Use pagination and batching for reads/queries (limit + skip or range queries with sort) to avoid scanning large collections in a single request; tune batchSize for cursor iteration.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, collect metrics (RU, latency, requestCharge), and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation via Azure Monitor / Log Analytics.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor RU usage, latency, request charges, index metrics, and slow queries; integrate with Azure monitoring/alerts and collect logs/metrics from MCP server tools for index/query plans.

practices.practice: Limit concurrency when calling external services (OpenAI) using an async semaphore or similar rate-limiter to bound simultaneous requests so you don't overwhelm external APIs or your pipeline.
practices.prior_belief: Limit concurrency when calling external services (OpenAI): use an async semaphore to bound simultaneous requests so you do not overwhelm the network or exceed throughput limits for the pipeline or the database.

practices.practice: Design enrichment/upsert pipelines to be idempotent: use a stable key and upsert operations so re-processing a review does not create duplicates or partial writes.
practices.prior_belief: Use idempotent processing: design the enrichment pipeline so that re-processing the same review (e.g., via upsert with a stable key) produces the same result and does not create duplicates or partial writes.

practices.practice: Use JSON schema validation ($jsonSchema) on collections where supported to enforce required fields and types, or validate in the application layer before writes.
practices.prior_belief: Define JSON schema validation on the collection (if supported) or validate in the application layer to ensure required fields (product_id, review_text) and types (sentiment_score numeric, tags array) before writing to the DB.

practices.practice: When using Beanie ODM, declare indexes in the Document Settings and call init_beanie once at application startup so indexes are created at initialization rather than per-request.
practices.prior_belief: When using Beanie ODM, declare indexes in the Document Settings and call init_beanie once at app startup with the database object rather than creating indexes ad-hoc on each request.

practices.practice: Prefer DocumentDB's `createSearchIndexes` + `$search` (BM25) full-text search path with search indexes and custom analyzers rather than the community `$text` approach when you need advanced full-text features; use hybrid BM25+vector approaches for combined lexical/semantic retrieval.

Pick a partition (shard) key with the right tradeoff: collocate related workloads (e.g., product-level data) on the same partition key for localized queries, choose high-cardinality keys for write-heavy workloads, and avoid hot/monotonic keys.
practices.prior_belief: Use database-level or container-level throughput grouping: collocate related collections/documents under the same partition key (e.g., product_id) to optimize hot partitions and RU distribution; choose partition key with high cardinality.

practices.practice: Enable built-in backups and retention and test restore procedures; for critical data export periodic snapshots to durable storage as part of your backup plan.
practices.prior_belief: Plan for backups and retention: enable built-in continuous or periodic backup and test restore procedures; for critical data, export periodic snapshots to durable storage.

practices.practice: Prefer extracting structured tags/key themes and indexing those tag fields for fast filtering/aggregation rather than relying solely on expensive free-text indexes when your queries are structured, but no authoritative Azure DocumentDB guidance explicitly mandates this trade-off.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid expensive text-search indexes unless required; prefer extracting structured tags/key themes (via OpenAI) and indexing those tags for fast filtering and aggregation instead of free-text queries.

practices.practice: Test pipelines end-to-end with a mockable OpenAI implementation in CI (DevProxy / local LLM / test doubles) so CI runs do not require real API keys and real external calls.
practices.prior_belief: Test the pipeline end-to-end with a mock OpenAI implementation and deterministic seeds so CI runs do not require real API keys; allow switching to real OpenAI via configuration only when running in a controlled environment.
